name: partial-hash-snapshot-treated-as-binding
title: Audit every consumer of the non-throwing evidence hash snapshot reader for partial snapshots treated as bindings
description: core/evidence-freshness.ts captureEvidenceHashSnapshot never throws for git or hash failures; it returns a snapshot whose headHash, materialHash and storyFilesHash are each OPTIONAL and simply omitted on failure, and tryCaptureEvidenceHashSnapshot only converts a thrown error into undefined. Story B-a745 finding F-022 (from an independent Codex host) showed that a consumer which treats any returned snapshot as available will present a plan bound to null digests without disclosing it; B-a745 fixed its own collector by classifying a snapshot missing any digest as hash_snapshot_unavailable with a bounded detail. The same reader is consumed elsewhere and those callers only distinguish thrown versus returned: packages/main/src/core/done-oracle.ts around line 286, packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts around line 628, packages/main/src/core/lifecycle-readiness.ts around line 853, packages/main/src/handlers/phase-gates.ts around line 834, and packages/main/src/handlers/session.ts around line 1416, as located by the F-022 implementer. done-oracle and phase-gates are lifecycle gate owners, so a partial snapshot accepted as a binding there could let a gate compare or record a null digest as if it were a real one. This story audits each caller, decides per site whether a partial snapshot must fail closed, be disclosed, or is genuinely tolerable, and adds a regression fixture per site. evidence-freshness.ts itself was protected in B-a745 and is where a shared missing-digest classifier should probably live.
